title: 5-HT2A receptors in layer 5 pyramidal neurons mediate the neuroplastic but not the hallucinogenic effects of psilocybin
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02490-yPsilocybin promotes and stabilizes new connections between neurons in the mouse cerebral cortex, especially after stress. Baker et al. show that 5-HT2A receptor signaling in layer 5 pyramidal neurons mediates this effect but is not required for a mouse behavioral proxy of hallucinations.

title: A half-center oscillator regulates sleep pressure
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02431-9Hasenhuetl et al. show that neurons innervating the dorsal fan-shaped body of Drosophila form a half-center oscillator, a circuit motif typically found in central pattern generators for locomotion. Here, this circuit generates slow-wave activity for the regulation of sleep.

title: An aging-sensitive secreted phospholipase confers neuroprotection and cognitive resilience
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02465-zThis study identifies a secreted phospholipase in the hippocampal dentate gyrus that mediates an aging-sensitive compensatory mechanism promoting cognitive resilience and neuroprotection.

title: Spatiotemporal AI-based modeling of gene regulation and variant effects in the developing human brain using Seal
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02470-2Seal is an artificial intelligence framework that predicts the effects of regulatory variants in 802 brain cell states, revealing spatiotemporal gene regulation and pinpointing cell types and developmental stages associated with neuropsychiatric conditions.

title: Periventricular gradient pathology is linked to ependymal reactivity and cell adhesion disruption in multiple sclerosis
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02461-3This study identifies ependymal dysfunction as a mechanism linking inflammatory cerebrospinal fluid to increased ventricular permeability and periventricular pathology in multiple sclerosis.

title: Ring attractor networks go full circle
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02394-xClark et al. demonstrate that heterogeneous data-driven models implement head-direction selectivity through the same dynamical principles as classical ring networks. In doing so, the authors reconcile biological realism with theoretical simplicity, unifying existing frameworks and broadening the space of connectivity structures to be searched in data.

title: Symmetries and continuous attractors in disordered neural circuits
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02452-4Head-direction cells are far more disorderly than classical continuous-attractor models allow. Clark et al. show that this disorder is nevertheless compatible with these models and that the underlying connectivity matrix hides a circular symmetry.
